clue.text: Saintly individual finishes off top fare at Safe Harbour

indicators.note: the finishes, or final letters, of the last five words are taken off and strung together

explanation.surface: A holy figure polishes off the last of the best food at a quayside restaurant called Safe Harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' takes the last letter of each of the five words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter, the apostle, is the best-known saintly individual of that name.

clue.text: Keep watch over son, knowing woman's set on daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece set on another sits above it in the answer

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
hep is an old slang word for knowing or in the know, a variant of hip
her is the pronoun for a woman; the 's stands for 'is', linking to what follows
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shrewd mother keeps an eye on her son while sitting on her daughter's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set on' places HER above D in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd is to guide and look after, as a shepherd watches over a flock.

clue.text: See 26
Selection of music at school show

indicators.note: Selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A school concert offers a selection of musical numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is the long-running Andrew Lloyd Webber musical, an example of a stage show.

clue.text: Born in hushed capital city

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for born inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet, so mum means hushed
capital as an exclamation means excellent, as does A1

explanation.surface: Someone born in a silenced capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is read as the old exclamation meaning first-rate, A1, written here as AI with the digit taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is India's largest city.

clue.text: No notice for adult who's done for infringement

indicators.note: done in the sense of beaten up or knocked about tells us to rearrange these letters
No says the following notice is taken away from the word adult

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A grown-up is punished for an offence without being warned first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No notice' removes AD from ADULT, leaving ULT; 'done' then shuffles FOR + ULT + WHO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a foul throw is an illegal throw-in, an infringement of the laws of the game.

clue.text: Through shimmering haze, suss a rich source of wisdom

indicators.note: Through says one set of letters runs through the middle of the other
something shimmering wavers and shifts, so the letters of haze are rearranged
to suss is to work out, here working the letters of a rich into a new order

explanation.surface: Peer through the heat haze and you might discover a wealthy source of knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shimmering' turns HAZE into ZE...AH, and 'suss' turns A RICH into CHARI, which 'Through' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Zechariah is an Old Testament prophet and book, so a scriptural source of wisdom.

clue.text: Don's pressing the snooze button to the left?

indicators.note: in an across entry reading to the left means reading backwards

parts.note: someone hitting snooze is still in bed, not up

explanation.surface: An Oxford don dozes on, jabbing the alarm's snooze button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university lecturer, but it is the verb meaning to dress in; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, the two being straight synonyms.

clue.text: South African brainpower cracks first half of Guardian cryptic

indicators.note: cracks says the brainpower breaks into the letters around it
cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so those letters are jumbled
the first half of the word Guardian is used, its first four letters

parts.note: IQ, the intelligence quotient, measures brainpower

explanation.surface: A clever South African solves the start of a Guardian crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' looks like it describes the crossword, but it is the anagram signal, making GRUA; 'cracks' then breaks it open.
explanation.definitionFit: The Griqua are a South African people of mixed descent, so a member is a South African.

clue.text: Wham!'s piano not initially needed in Cornwall local

indicators.note: piano, not the letter that follows, says one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: Kernow is the Cornish-language name for Cornwall, the local word for it

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word needed

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: The pop duo Wham! are told their piano is not needed for a gig in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Wham! looks like the band; it is the comic-book sound effect. 'not initially needed' means the piano letter stands in for N in KERNOW, Cornwall's name in Cornish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerpow and wham are both comic-strip exclamations representing the noise of a blow.

clue.text: Anagram Bible snatcher not in the crossword game!

indicators.note: Anagram tells us outright to rearrange the letters of Bible snatcher
not says the letters of the words in the are left out of that pool

explanation.surface: A thief takes a Bible, but not in the word game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anagram ... not' rearranges BIBLE SNATCHER after taking out the letters of IN THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the board game in which players build interlocking words on a grid.

clue.text: Absence felt as cherished mother wings away

parts.note: something cherished is dear to you

indicators.note: the wings of mother are its two outer letters at each end, which are taken away

explanation.surface: A beloved mother's absence is felt as she flies away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings away' strips two letters from each side of MOTHER, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, an absence of something needed.

clue.text: Short vacation? Essentially, Jamie's occupying flats near river

indicators.note: occupying puts that letter inside the word for the vacation

parts.note: hols is short for holidays, a vacation

indicators.note: Essentially takes the essence, the central letter, of the name Jamie

explanation.surface: On a brief holiday, Jamie stays in flats beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' means low-lying land, not apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: A holm is a piece of flat, low ground by a river, often flooded.

clue.text: Ending fast early, what about … this?

indicators.note: Ending, with early, says the final letter comes off the word for fast
the ending is taken away early, before the word finishes

parts.note: fast means quick

indicators.note: about turns the exclamation round

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: Someone ending a fast ahead of schedule asks what about eating this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a dish offered to someone breaking their fast early. 'Ending ... early' drops the K from QUICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiche is a savoury egg tart, the dish suggested to break the fast.

clue.text: In five, could it be doctor's calling?

parts.note: being in means being at home
V is the Roman numeral for five
is it? asks could it be?

explanation.surface: A worried patient wonders whether, out of five, this could be the doctor's vocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' looks like vocation; it is a doctor calling at a patient's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A home visit is when a doctor calls at the patient's house rather than seeing them at the surgery.

clue.text: Use love where Christians place trust?

indicators.note: where says the letter is placed in the thing named next, as trust is placed in God

parts.note: Christians place their trust in God
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction to use love, which is where Christians put their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' is the noun, as in 'it's no good' meaning 'it's no use'.
explanation.definitionFit: Good and use are interchangeable in phrases such as 'no good' and 'no use', meaning benefit.

clue.text: For fermentation of Beaujolais, I present this lady as OBE

indicators.note: fermentation stirs up the wine, so the letters of Beaujolais are rearranged; the answer plus the other words make up that pool

explanation.surface: A wine merchant presents a lady with her OBE over a glass of Beaujolais.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BEAUJOLAIS, worked up by 'For fermentation of', give the answer together with AS and OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Julia is a woman's name, so it can stand for a particular lady.

clue.text: Can you tell me — roughly speaking — USA's most northerly state capital?

indicators.note: roughly speaking says the casual question, said loosely, gives the sound of the answer

parts.note: d'you know? asks can you tell me?

explanation.surface: A quiz question: can you tell me, more or less, the capital of America's most northern state?
explanation.definitionFit: Juneau is the capital of Alaska, the northernmost US state, so it lies farthest north of all state capitals.

clue.text: Can't we tell who this singer is from behind?

indicators.note: from behind means reading the letters backwards

parts.note: if we cannot tell who someone is, there is no ID

explanation.surface: Fans wonder whether they can identify a singer seen only from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Celine Dion is the Canadian singer known for My Heart Will Go On.

clue.text: Just like devoted couple to stage an upcoming charitable activity

indicators.note: to stage, here meaning to host, has the doting word take in the reversed article

parts.note: a devoted couple are doting on each other

indicators.note: in a down entry upcoming means reading upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A loving pair, just like newlyweds, put on a forthcoming charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' and 'upcoming' read as putting on a show soon; here 'upcoming' turns the article round in this down entry, and 'to stage' houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Donating means giving to good causes, an activity of charity.

clue.text: Actor Paul (unlike actor Gary!) a reformed character

definitions.meaning: Paul ... was the Hollywood star of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
a ... is someone who has changed for the better

explanation.surface: Paul Newman, unlike Gary Oldman, has turned over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a joke: Gary Oldman's surname splits as OLD MAN, the opposite of NEW MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Newman is the surname of the actor; split, it gives a new man, someone reformed.

clue.text: Commotion with gull circling field next to river

indicators.note: circling has the gull go all the way round the commotion

parts.note: a mew is a gull, especially the common gull
ado means fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A noisy fuss as a gull wheels over a riverside field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often low-lying water meadow beside a river.

clue.text: Well, now!

definitions.meaning: a natural source of water, like a well

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, now!' reads as a single exclamation of surprise, but it holds two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a water source, and spring is also the current season when the puzzle was published.

clue.text: What repels an aficionado of Scripture?

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject once called Scripture
a buff is an enthusiast or aficionado

explanation.surface: A question asking what puts off someone keen on the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'an RE buff', the aficionado of Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a blunt refusal, something that drives away or repulses an approach.

clue.text: Turned up churchyard feature belonging to Du Maurier's home

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: yew trees are a common feature of English churchyards
of means belonging to

explanation.surface: A yew tree in a churchyard turns up at Daphne du Maurier's house.
explanation.walkthrough: FOWEY is a small harbour town in Cornwall where the novelist Daphne du Maurier lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Daphne du Maurier made her home in Fowey, the Cornish town that inspired her novels.

clue.text: The Sun, say, apparently unable to move father's home?

indicators.note: apparently says the paper looks as if it is held inside the tool

parts.note: something held fast in a vice cannot move
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, an example of a rag, a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: The tabloid sun seems stuck at the house of a father.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'father' is a priest, so the home is a vicar's.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar, a parish priest addressed as Father.

clue.text: Paper cross worn by one closing coffee morning

indicators.note: worn by places the cross within the letters that follow, as if it were a necklace
closing takes the last letter of the word coffee

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A newspaper says a cross was worn by someone at the end of a coffee morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one closing coffee' is the last letter of COFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam paper is the written test sat by candidates.

clue.text: Dunce in art class presenting 'Chest of Future Bride'?!

definitions.meaning: the worst at drawing in an art class is the ...
where a young woman stores linen and items for married life, a hope chest

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: bottom of the class plus someone who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottom drawer is the collection of household linen a woman keeps ready for marriage, a trousseau chest.

clue.text: Dramatist succeeded: your compiler's in business!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
your compiler is the setter, who says I am, contracted to I'm
on means operating or in action, as a shop is on

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that a playwright made it and that he is open for business.
explanation.walkthrough: Pairs with the next clue: Simon and Garfunkel.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Simon was the American playwright of The Odd Couple.

clue.text: Art and rhythmic music by 'Nimrod' man on a loop

indicators.note: on a loop says letters cycle round from the end back to the start

parts.note: funk is a strongly rhythmic style of popular music
Elgar composed Nimrod, the Enigma Variations movement; he is also the setter

explanation.surface: Art goes with music playing the composer of Nimrod over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is Art Garfunkel. 'on a loop' moves the last three letters of FUNKELGAR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Garfunkel is the singer from Simon and Garfunkel, so his forename defines his surname.
